name: Shamyana Restaurant
why_it_matters: Boulevard's most consistent wazwan kitchen — currently #4 of 258 Srinagar restaurants on TripAdvisor with 4,750+ reviews. The full tarami (copper-platter feast) is served à la carte rather than as a fixed seven-course, which makes it accessible to two-person tables.
insider_tip: Ask for the lake-facing window on the upper floor; the ground floor is functional but doesn't deliver the Dal view that justifies coming to Boulevard. Trout fry is the dish to order if it's your one Kashmiri meal.
signature_address: Ghat No.2, Boulevard Road, Opposite Dal Lake, Dal Gate, Srinagar 190001

name: Bistro Boulevard by Pincer Foods
why_it_matters: Pincer Foods runs Bistro Boulevard as the Boulevard's go-to dessert-and-coffee stop — the cheesecake counter (blueberry, strawberry, cherry) is the local benchmark. Two decades on the strip.
insider_tip: Skip the dinner menu, which is decent but not why you came. Come at 4pm for cheesecake-and-coffee with a Dal Lake view from the upstairs window. Parking on Boulevard is impossible — walk from Ghat 9.
signature_address: Ghat No.9, Boulevard Road, Near Hotel New Park, Srinagar 190001

name: Winterfell Cafe
why_it_matters: India's first Game of Thrones-themed cafe — opened by cousins Kamran and Ummar Nisar, part of the wave of Kashmiri returnees building the Boulevard cafe scene post-2017. Stone-clad interiors, GoT memorabilia, a replica Iron Throne; rated 4.3 on TripAdvisor with #19 of 154 ranking.
insider_tip: It's a cafe-not-a-restaurant — come for coffee and a pizza, not a full meal. The terrace photographs better than the indoor seating; ask for the Iron Throne table if it's free.
signature_address: Boulevard Road, Opposite Ghat No.5, Srinagar 190001

name: Cafe Emerald
signature_dish: veg thali with kashmiri dum aloo
why_it_matters: The vegetarian counterpoint to Boulevard's wazwan-heavy strip. Pure-veg, value-priced, and well-positioned at Ghat 1 — the option for families travelling with vegetarian relatives or visitors keeping satvik on a Vaishno Devi yatra circuit.
insider_tip: Order the Kashmiri dum aloo — it's the only veg dish on Boulevard that captures the local cooking technique. The pizzas are competent but skippable.
signature_address: The Boulevard, Opposite Ghat No.1, Srinagar 190001

name: The Chinar — The LaLiT Grand Palace
why_it_matters: The dining room at The LaLiT Grand Palace, originally built in 1910 by Maharaja Pratap Singh as his Srinagar palace and converted to a hotel in the 20th century. The kitchen serves the most controlled wazwan in Srinagar — chef-curated rather than à la carte — with views over the palace lawn down to Dal Lake.
insider_tip: If you only want one wazwan in Srinagar and you're willing to pay for it, this is the proper sit-down version. Book the wazwan platter (₹3,000-ish per head) at least four hours ahead — it's slow-cooked and they need notice.
signature_address: The LaLiT Grand Palace, Gupkar Road, Dal Gate, Srinagar 190001

name: Nigeen Lake View Resort Restaurant
why_it_matters: The Boulevard strip is loud and tourist-saturated; Nigeen Lake (the quieter sibling lake to the north) has a fraction of the foot traffic. This resort restaurant is the only consistent public lakeside dining option on Nigeen, with a deck that sits directly over the water.
insider_tip: Nigeen-side dining is best at lunch when the light hits the lake from the east. Ask for the deck table; the indoor restaurant is just a hotel dining room without the view that makes the trip across town worth it.
